results.primary_cause: Evidence is conflicting: Capesize rates reached a two-year high on demand and tightening supply, but BIMCO reporting indicates that apparent 2026 strength may be substantially driven by temporary rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut. The durability and exact breadth of the cycle remain unresolved.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that the apparent strength of the 2026 dry-bulk market was substantially artificial from forced rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry Bulk Shipping Faces 2027 Supply Glut: BIMCO Warns Hormuz Rerouting Boost Will Reverse
